points.description: States that Bligh's theory makes no distinction between horizontal and vertical creep (seepage path) lengths, i.e. treats them as equally effective / simply adds them together.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the answer only says vaguely that the creep length is calculated wrongly or that horizontal and vertical parts are treated simply/the same without clear mention, or mentions only one of horizontal/vertical.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for the idea that Bligh treats horizontal and vertical creep lengths the same (no distinction, total length only), in any wording. Give 1 mark for a vague or partial answer, e.g. mentions only that creep length is considered as a total/straight path or only one of horizontal/vertical. Give 0 for unrelated drawbacks, such as ignoring uplift pressure alone with no mention of creep length treatment.
